The Promise of an Understandable Intelligence

Yannick Fontan · Original text from the YouTube description.

Symbolic Reasoning Agent An experimental journey through ARC-AGI 3 Episode 1 • Legacy Game LS20 The Promise of an Understandable Intelligence, Or How to Think Outside the Black Box.

For decades, we have asked artificial intelligence to produce the right answers. But what if we have been asking the wrong question? What if the real challenge is not producing the right answer... ...but understanding why it is the right answer? We are entering an era in which machines can predict, complete, generate, and optimize with extraordinary efficiency. Yet one fundamental question remains. Do they truly understand what they are doing? Or are they simply recognizing statistical regularities hidden within an ocean of data? I believe the next revolution in artificial intelligence will not be a revolution of scale. It will be a revolution of understanding. A truly intelligent system should not only be capable of acting. It should also be capable of explaining its reasoning. Visible to itself. Visible to human beings. Visible to those who will one day have to trust it. Because an intelligence that cannot explain its reasoning remains a black box, no matter how impressive its performance.

What you are seeing on the screen today is an environment from ARC-AGI 3. ARC is a collection of small interactive worlds created by François Chollet to explore one fundamental question: How can an intelligence learn to understand an entirely new world? There are no natural language instructions. No predefined knowledge. No explanations. Only an unfamiliar environment. Observe. Explore. Understand. For many researchers, ARC is simply a benchmark. For me, it is something much more profound. It is a laboratory for understanding.

For the past several months, I have been using this laboratory to explore a different path. A path that does not merely seek the correct answer. A path that seeks to make reasoning itself visible. This path has a name. Symbolic reasoning. Symbolic reasoning is not about finding statistical correlations. It is about manipulating concepts. Building hypotheses. Discovering relationships. Planning exploration. Drawing conclusions. Learning from evidence. And above all... explaining why an action makes sense. I believe this capability will become essential if we hope to build artificial intelligence that deserves our trust.

The project I am presenting today is therefore not simply an attempt to solve ARC puzzles. It is an attempt to build an architecture where every perception can become a concept. Every concept a belief. Every belief a hypothesis. Every hypothesis an exploration. And every exploration new knowledge. An architecture where reasoning no longer disappears behind millions, or even trillions, of parameters. An architecture where reasoning becomes... Observable. Manipulable. Verifiable. And ultimately... Understandable.

This series of videos will document that construction. Step by step. From the first foundations to a complete symbolic reasoning architecture. I am not claiming to present an Artificial General Intelligence today. I am proposing something more fundamental. The beginning of an exploration into what it truly means... to understand. Because I believe that intelligence should not be measured solely by its ability to predict. It should also be measured by its ability to make its own reasoning intelligible. And I believe one of the greatest challenges of our generation is precisely this: To make artificial intelligence understandable.

True science is not the one that predicts. It is the one that explains.
